item.title: Selling to Agents — metered data for buyers that don't have eyes
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Three saves describe one gap. Quality publishers block AI crawlers, so AI search cites whatever is left. AI assistants favor the sponsored option in 18 of 23 models, so they are steerable buyers. Software is going headless, so agents pick tools by speed, cost and accuracy instead of interface. x402 revives HTTP 402 so an agent can pay a stablecoin micropayment per request. A one-person owner of…

item.title: One Dancer, a Thousand Bodies — Ensemble Choreography from Herd Physics
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Crystal Pite's ensemble pieces make dozens of dancers move like one organism, and that takes a company and months of rehearsal. Now webcam mocap captures one dancer, text-to-motion models spin out variations, and the quant collection's Ising herding model supplies the missing rule: one temperature knob that moves a crowd from noise to sudden collective turns. That last step is a market model…

item.title: Mocap as Reward — teaching cheap robots to move like you
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: The Microduck RL demo shows the classic failure: a loose reward function makes the robot 'stand' in a way nobody intended. The catalog also holds the fix, scattered across collections. FreeMoCap turns a webcam into markerless motion capture, HY-Motion produces motion from text on robot skeletons, and Blender plus a GPU contact solver can rehearse physical contact. Use captured or generated…

item.title: Who's Across the Table — forensics for the system trading against you
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Across the catalog, the systems you interact with are quietly optimizing against you: a puzzle game runs an on-device XGBoost model to time difficulty to your ad value, overnight and intraday returns run as a decades-long sawtooth, a bedroom spoofer tripped depth-reading algorithms in the 2010 Flash Crash, wash trading inflates crypto volume, and exchanges sold speed to HFTs. Agent-plus-Ghidra…

item.title: Real CLAUDE.md Examples, Annotated
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Anthropic's own guidance is short, and most of the good public files follow it whether they cite it or not.

item.title: The Album Is a Device Again — Offline Generative Music Objects
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Tristan Perich already shipped a symphony as a chip in a CD case. Google's Gemma Translator shows a full speech model stack running offline on a Pi 5 with a printable case and parts list. Local voice cloning fits in 100M parameters, and memory LCDs sip power. Put those together and a song can be a small object that performs a slightly different take every time it plays — the artist's own voice…

item.title: The AI Capex Stack — reading it like a credit analyst
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: An ex-Morgan Stanley structurer explains that CoreWeave-style GPU loans have a thin tail: loan, contract and GPU useful life are nearly the same length, so the bull case rests on hourly rental prices after contracts end. Other saves price that number from the demand side: open weights flipped to about 80% of token volume in 12 weeks, DeepSeek serves near-frontier agents at $0.28 per million…

item.title: Mission Control for 80 Agents — Conway's law meets game UI
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Once you run more than a handful of agents, the bottleneck is your attention, not tokens. Creative technologists are already prototyping the answer without naming it — Bot Crossing puts 80 agents on a tiny planet where they raise hands for help, AgentCraft runs them as Minecraft workers in isolated worktrees, a TouchDesigner sketch commands agents by gesture, a Quest 3 canvas directs them…

item.title: Capture the Room Twice — Splat Scans and Song for Roots Music
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Roots musicians already treat the room as an instrument — testing a 200-year-old house's resonance, filming tunes on porches and in old venues, the way Lomax filmed singers in their own kitchens. A phone can now capture that room as a Gaussian splat, and Gausseous makes the splat react to audio in a browser. Record the room's acoustics in the same session and the sound and the image come from…

item.title: Napkin Sketch → Production Asset: The 5-Tool Creative Pipeline
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: A hand-drawn sketch can become a production-ready 3D animation in under an hour by chaining Procreate → Magnific AI → 3DAI Studio → Move AI → final render. Each tool handles one transformation step.

item.title: Own the Thermometer — $100 sensors as prediction-market edge
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: A student cleared $100K+ on Polymarket weather contracts with a dorm-built weather station, and a separate trader harvests contracts already sitting at 99c. Put those next to free real-time feeds (NASA EONET, SDR-received weather satellite images, public EIA/HIFLD infrastructure data, live plane and ship layers) and the pattern is clear — the edge on event contracts is not a smarter model, it is…

item.title: Dox Yourself First — a scheduled agent that runs the OSINT kit on you
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: The catalog saved a full attacker toolkit — Sherlock and Alien's Eye for usernames, email-to-account mappers, deleted-Reddit recovery, GeoSpy geolocating photos from plants and shadows — next to the defense: a de-dox checklist written after Meta AI inferred a creator's home from old posts, a data-broker opt-out game, the Flock plate-search transparency site. An agent with a weekly cron can run…

item.title: Scan, Fit, Print — agents that design parts around real objects
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Open-source scanners (a smartphone Orbiter rig, a Raspberry Pi handheld LiDAR, LingBot-Map's video-to-3D) now produce a usable mesh of the thing you need to fit. LLMs already write Blender Python, and they can build a CLI for any app that has no MCP. Point the agent at the scan, have it write parametric CAD that references the scanned surfaces, and you get a custom-fit part on the first print…

item.title: Physics Models → Market Alpha: When Scientists Become Traders
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: 26 posts map physics/math models to trading — avalanche theory, Ising models, phase space reconstruction. The meta-insight: the quant edge isn't in finance, it's in importing models from other fields.

item.title: Forecast the Weather, Not the Price — gating models by tradeability
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Open candlestick foundation models like Kronos give you a forecast on every bar, and a hedge-fund stress test says it fails on many levels. A separate save shows the better question: a small logistic regression that predicts tomorrow's efficiency ratio (trend versus chop) and skips the choppy days lifted almost every metric over two years out of sample. Physics-flavored measures in the quant…

item.title: Anything With Geometry — Ink on Paper: the Pen-Plotter Loop
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Fogleman's ln turns any 3D scene into hidden-line vector paths, and vpype makes those paths plotter-ready. Everything else in the catalog that produces geometry — a phone scan, a ripped PS1 level, a ray-marched fractal, a strange attractor, the phase-space shape of BTC volatility, a Blender scene an agent wrote in Python — becomes a source for that one pipe. The output is a physical ink…

item.title: Strategy Autoresearch — the judge is the product, not the agent
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Self-rewriting loops (Karpathy-style autoresearch, bilevel coach loops, Microsoft SkillOpt) keep any edit that beats a benchmark. Point one at trading and it becomes an industrial overfitting machine — the backtest is the benchmark, and the loop will beat it ten thousand times. The quant saves already hold the fix: probability of backtest overfitting, permutation tests, transaction costs and…

item.title: Offline AI Appliances — one job, one box, no cloud
item.dc:creator: DejaViewed
item.description: Gemma Translator puts speech recognition, translation and TTS on a Raspberry Pi 5, and it ships with a bill of materials and a printable case. Around it, the catalog holds a 100M-parameter local voice cloner, a 3B OCR model that reads 100-page PDFs in one pass, local video search over dashcam footage, 4GB-GPU fine-tuning, and 27B agent models on one 24GB card. Together these are a parts bin for…

item.title: Claude Opus 5.5 to Blender — 3D animation built entirely as code
item.dc:creator: nateherkai
item.description: Claude Opus 5.5 wrote everything: a web mock of the After Effects UI, a Python script that builds the Blender scene, the character animation, plus the music and sound effects. Blender rendered 360 frames on GPU in about 15 minutes and FFmpeg stitched the video. Full prompt is comment-gated.

item.title: Claude Code vs smart TV — stripping bloatware over local WiFi
item.dc:creator: chase.h.ai
item.description: Short clip on pointing Claude Code at a smart TV on the same WiFi network to remove bloatware and customize it, with before/after speed comparisons. The prompt is shown but no device specifics or method details are given.

item.title: EMA9 + VWAP crossover — automated 3-minute options strategy pitch
item.dc:creator: timhutter.official
item.description: Promo for the RoboQuant platform: buy calls or puts when EMA9 crosses VWAP on the 3-minute chart, with a claimed $179k month and 79.9% prop-challenge pass rate. The backtest claims are unverified marketing, though the crossover rule itself is a simple, testable baseline.

item.title: Nintendo static recompilation — native Zelda and Mario Kart ports
item.dc:creator: quickfinesse
item.description: Static recompilation projects turn Switch games into native apps: Tears of the Kingdom on Apple Silicon Mac and iPhone (~90fps on a MacBook Air), Skyward Sword HD on Windows, Linux, Steam Deck and Mac at 60fps/4K with a mod manager, and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on iPhone/Mac with online play. Bring your own game copy.

item.title: REA MCP — agent-driven reverse engineering with a Ghidra backend
item.dc:creator: backsla.sh
item.description: REA is an MCP server that lets an AI agent reverse engineer apps and stripped native binaries, with Ghidra doing the decompilation while the agent drives and cites evidence per call. The creator decompiled a closed-source program in three to four minutes on Ubuntu. Setup is deferred to a follow-up video.

item.title: Claude ambition prompt — four knobs to make AI aim higher
item.dc:creator: chase.h.ai
item.description: Covers a post by Claude's lead engineer on tuning AI ambition along speed, altitude, depth and range. The appendable prompt asks Claude what a top professional would do that you didn't ask for, what raw material they'd start from, which methods and tools they'd use, and who besides you would judge the result, then rewrites the prompt to ask for exactly that.

item.title: Duss.o Labs 'Wobbles' — procedural Blender loop scored in Ableton
item.dc:creator: d__u__s__s__o_____l__a__b__s
item.description: LAB/018, an experimental procedural animation made in Blender with a self-produced Ableton soundtrack. Pure visual reference, no process breakdown.

item.title: Mandelbulb — ray-marching a 3D fractal from z⁸ + c
item.dc:creator: elemental.math
item.description: Explains the Mandelbulb: Daniel White's spherical-coordinate trick for 3D 'multiplication', raised to power 8 by Paul Nylander, rendered by ray marching with the distance estimate d = ½·r·log r/dr. Code is ported line by line from Mandelbulber's GPL-3.0 source, with the Hamilton 'multiply triplets' history as a bonus.

item.title: CoreWeave debt explained — how GPU-backed loans fund the neoclouds
item.dc:creator: thewallstreetskinny
item.description: An ex-Morgan Stanley CDO structurer explains the neocloud stack (landlords, vertically integrated players like IREN and Crusoe, CoreWeave, Nebius) and why CoreWeave's GPU-backed asset financing spooked markets. Advance rates hit 90-95% against off-taker credit, and loan, contract and GPU useful life are nearly the same length, leaving a thin tail.

item.title: Block Blast reverse-engineered — on-device XGBoost rigs difficulty for ad revenue
item.dc:creator: ayoships
item.description: A reverse engineer found Block Blast runs a local XGBoost model on device signals (phone model, country, past ad revenue, vibration setting) to predict your ad value and adjust difficulty. Rules like 'Boost Then Kill' and 'High Value Ad Harvest' trigger a 'death algorithm' right when a pricey revive ad is ready. Full code evidence is promised later on the creator's site.

item.title: Headless software + MCP — Chamath on why software IP stops being a moat
item.dc:creator: atlasberry008
item.description: Breaks down Chamath's All-In claim that software IP is worthless once services go headless and agents call them via MCP. With Salesforce and xAI's Grok exposing headless engines, agents pick tools on speed, cost or accuracy, so the interface stops being the moat.

item.title: Claudex skill — Claude and GPT-6 Astra cross-audit plan and build
item.dc:creator: nateherkai
item.description: A free skill that splits work between two frontier models: Claude writes the plan and GPT-6 Astra audits it until it holds, then roles swap so Astra builds and Claude audits. Runs inside Claude or Codex as a reusable skill.

item.title: Reverse Engineer Anything — trending repo that explains how any app works
item.dc:creator: theericmichaud
item.description: The week's top trending GitHub repo, about 70k stars: point Claude Code or Codex at an app and it explains how the feature is built so you can rebuild it. Users have revived old hardware, e.g. a Logitech keypad on Linux in 15 minutes, plus scanners and sound cards that lost drivers.

item.title: Game decompilation with AI — which reconstruction methods stay legal
item.dc:creator: lizthedeveloper
item.description: Covers five decompilation approaches (matching decompilation, functional reconstruction, static recompilation, engine re-implementation, porting recovered source) and argues engine re-implementation and functional reconstruction are the legal paths. AI fits because the original game's GPU pixel output is a verifiable oracle for rewriting the engine in a new language.

item.title: ChatGPT Astra 6 — comment-gated SEO ranking link
item.dc:creator: socialtypro
item.description: Engagement bait praising ChatGPT Astra 6 for SEO with a comment-to-get-link hook. The transcript has no content.

item.title: AI game decompilation hype — Mario/Halo merges and PS5 piracy rumors
item.dc:creator: pokeswaggshop
item.description: Rumor-heavy rant claiming AI decompilation is letting people merge games like Mario 64 and Halo, pirate Adobe software, port the PS5 library to PC, and leak GTA 6. Mostly unverified claims plus a piracy justification, with no technical detail.

item.title: Self-improving trading agent — critic loop that rewrites losing strategies
item.dc:creator: raycfu
item.description: Workflow pitch: describe a strategy, an agent codes it and wires the broker API, runs a five-year backtest, and a critic agent dissects losing trades and rewrites entry/exit logic before rerunning. Hard-coded stop-loss and drawdown limits sit outside the agent's reach, and failed strategies go to a local DB the agent learns from. Guide is comment-gated.

item.title: AI networking for job referrals — archetype-based LinkedIn outreach
item.dc:creator: angus.sewell
item.description: Have an AI export your LinkedIn connections, find newly hired or promoted people via a sales data tool, classify each into four personality archetypes from their profile and posts, then draft outreach tailored to each. Prompts are comment-gated.

item.title: Google game Playground — why a harness that can't see its output fails
item.dc:creator: nateherkai
item.description: A hands-on review of Google's prompt-to-game Playground: output ignored the supplied concept art, the model denied receiving it, and it admitted it cannot see or play the games it builds. The takeaway is that a game-building harness needs visual verification and playtesting.

item.title: Abliterated Qwen 3.5 9B — run PewDiePie-style Ajax locally with llama.cpp
item.dc:creator: codrkai
item.description: Walkthrough of running an abliterated Qwen 3.5 9B GGUF (the base of PewDiePie's Ajax model) locally: download from Hugging Face, install llama.cpp via Homebrew, start llama-server with context size and port, then point the DeepSeek harness at the custom endpoint. Also mentions PewDiePie's Odysseus agent harness.

item.title: AgentCraft — Minecraft mod where Claude agents write real code
item.dc:creator: itsnicconley
item.description: An open-source Minecraft mod built on Claude's agent system: a Foreman tracks tasks, ordering, decisions and inter-agent messages, workers each get an isolated copy of the code, and nothing merges until approved. Agents commit under their own names and can be messaged mid-task, and they walk over to find you when they need input.

item.title: Open vs closed token share — Friedberg on the 12-week flip and Anthropic risk
item.dc:creator: techno.optimist.prime
item.description: David Friedberg on All-In says token usage flipped from 80/20 closed-to-open to 80/20 open-to-closed in 12 weeks, calling it Anthropic's biggest risk factor ahead of S-1s. He expects a bifurcated market: open weights for most use, premium models for hard engineering, math and biology work.

item.title: Quake III fast inverse square root — the 0x5f3759df bit hack explained
item.dc:creator: mygearhut
item.description: Explains Quake III's four-line fast inverse square root: reinterpret float bits as an integer (which behaves logarithmically), shift right to halve the exponent, subtract from magic constant 0x5f3759df, then one Newton-Raphson step to bring error under 0.175%. Covers why normalization was costly on 1999 Pentiums and the constant's lineage through 3dfx and Cleve Moler.

item.title: Overnight vs intraday returns — Knuteson's 'Strikingly Suspicious' anomaly
item.dc:creator: quantpapers
item.description: Bruce Knuteson (ex-MIT physicist, D. E. Shaw) splits each day into close-to-open and open-to-close: Micron since 1990 is +138M% overnight and -99.9% intraday, and the same sawtooth shows in 21 indices (China reversed). His paper 'Strikingly Suspicious Overnight and Intraday Returns' rejects earnings and news as explanations and alleges large firms push prices at the open; it's a claim, not a…

item.title: Efficiency-ratio forecaster — skip choppy days to lift a strategy's metrics
item.dc:creator: telonicstrading
item.description: Instead of predicting direction, a logistic regression on 15 price features forecasts the next day's Kaufman efficiency ratio (trendiness versus chop). Trades on predicted low-efficiency days made about a third of the money, so gating them out improved nearly every metric and held on two years of out-of-sample data.

item.title: Five Python 1DTE options bots — visualized as a live trading city
item.dc:creator: nickafischer
item.description: A trader runs five rule-based Python bots on QQQ, SPY and IWM one-day-to-expiry options, visualized as a city where each tower shows signals and fires on call/put entries. Strategies are 'trending' and 'OG' with a daily profit lock. P&L claims ($72k in a month) are unverified.

item.title: Whop neobank blueprint — one-click fintech with cards and crypto rails
item.dc:creator: chase.h.ai
item.description: Sponsored Whop promo: a 'neobank blueprint' that spins up virtual cards, balances, crypto deposits, payouts and transfers, with fees you collect per swipe or transfer. Framed as cloning Coinbase in five minutes, which it is not.

item.title: Regular Show's 'Synth Wars' — synthesizer battle as cosmic boss fight
item.dc:creator: electronicmusic.official
item.description: The climax of Regular Show's 'Gary's Synthesizer', where two half-brothers settle a throne dispute with a synth battle (discord vs harmony) that escalates into a cosmic boss fight. Fun reference for music-driven animated set pieces.

item.title: GLM-5.3 Hugging Face takedown — Pirate Face mirrors and model access fights
item.dc:creator: wassimyounes_
item.description: News mix: Hugging Face disabled a modified GLM-5.3 listing and Pirate Face claims a decentralized mirror. PewDiePie reports OpenAI bans while distilling his Ajax model, and Anthropic research says GLM-5.3 approached Claude Mythos Preview on exploit-development tests. The video pushes cracked-model links, so treat with caution.

item.title: Founder OS — 17 always-on AI agents running a one-person business
item.dc:creator: brodyautomates
item.description: Tour of a custom Founder OS dashboard: 17 agents on a Mac Mini covering comms, sales, finance, marketing and clients, with a skills tree, task panel, workflow builder, Trackio lead attribution and a 'wizard' conductor agent. The base Founder OS is described as open source with a waitlist.

item.title: ln + vpype — 3D scenes to hidden-line vector art for pen plotters
item.dc:creator: index.opensource
item.description: Michael Fogleman's ln (Go) renders 3D scenes as 2D vector paths by ray-testing each path segment for visibility, supporting CSG, math surfaces and procedural cities. vpype then merges and sorts paths for plotting, cutting pen-up travel 86% in this example. Both MIT licensed, output straight to SVG.

item.title: Impeccable skill + Three.js — three-part stack for premium AI-built websites
item.dc:creator: tenfoldmarc
item.description: Recipe for one-shot polished websites with Claude: the Impeccable skill (generate variations then refine with its 23 design sub-skills), an image or video generator such as GPT Image 2.5 or Seedance 2.5 for visuals, and Three.js for smooth animation and transitions.

item.title: Anti-surveillance OPSEC tools — plate-reader confusion and photo poisoning
item.dc:creator: carterperez.dev
item.description: Three privacy tools: license-plate marks that make Flock and ALPR cameras misread your plate, an image cloaking tool that poisons photos against face models and deepfakes, and a list of 78 ranked ways to evade AI surveillance. Links are comment-gated. Note that altering plates is illegal in many places.

item.title: Agent Reach — open-source skill letting agents read Reddit and X
item.dc:creator: itstundeanthony
item.description: An open-source repo installed as a Claude skill that gives agents access to 13 platforms without API costs. The demo shows Claude failing to fetch a Reddit post and an X thread, then succeeding with comments once Agent Reach is installed.

item.title: Five fringe GitHub repos — WiFi sensing, offline 400B LLM, satellite capture
item.dc:creator: cracked.artificial
item.description: A hype-framed listicle of open-source projects: RuView turns WiFi into a through-wall person sensor, Flash MoE runs a 400B model on an iPhone offline, a walk-through camera tool builds 3D replicas of buildings, an app detects nearby camera glasses, and a cheap dish plus SDR pulls live weather-satellite images. Repo links are comment-gated.

item.title: Claude trading watcher — LiquidTrade + QuiverQuant for insider-trade alerts
item.dc:creator: nateherkai
item.description: Connect Claude to LiquidTrade for brokerage access across stocks, crypto, forex and prediction markets, and QuiverQuant for insider, politician and institutional trade data. Then give it a rule like tracking an investor's disclosures, compare against your portfolio, run it as a recurring routine, and paper trade first.

item.title: Jev keyword triage — score SERP beatability before writing content
item.dc:creator: olivermerrick___
item.description: Pull the top 10 results for 72 keywords and have TypeSafe's Jev (a classifier model that returns probabilities) answer literal questions per result: intent match, depth, freshness, site strength, beatable or not. Three or more weak results means target the keyword, then Claude writes. 720 results cost about 4 cents, search volume still needs a separate tool.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra side hustles — ten money-making uses, no detail
item.dc:creator: raycfu
item.description: A silent video promising ten ways to make money with GPT-6 Astra. No transcript or slide text survives, so there is nothing to act on.

item.title: Chat-history mining — derive better custom instructions from your AI logs
item.dc:creator: angus.sewell
item.description: Export your full ChatGPT or Claude history, have a small model like Jev tag every conversation for mistakes and usage patterns, then feed the analysis to your main assistant to write new custom instructions. A cheaper alternative to building a full personal 'Jarvis' agent.

item.title: Browser spy-satellite OSINT map — 19 live layers with voice control
item.dc:creator: carterperez.dev
item.description: A trending GitHub repo offering a 3D browser globe with 19 live data layers like public CCTV, Flock camera locations and traffic, plus a Jarvis-style voice interface. You can fly to a city or click a live flight to view a simulated cockpit perspective. Link is comment-gated.

item.title: Open-source AI week — OpenViking, ARTEMIS, GLM-5.3 FlashX, Unsloth Studio
item.dc:creator: drcintas
item.description: Six releases in 60 seconds: OpenViking (context database for agent memory), Google's ARTEMIS (prompt-to-phone automation over MCP for Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity), PrismML Ternary Bonsai 2 (27B ternary reasoning model, 262k context), AWS Pizza Bot (email-style inbox for background agents), Z.ai GLM-5.3 FlashX (320B multimodal, 1M context, local), and Unsloth Studio no-code fine-tuning of…

item.title: GitHub URL swaps — gitdiagram, gitingest, deepwiki and gitmcp for any repo
item.dc:creator: ariacodez
item.description: Swap github.com in a repo URL for gitdiagram.com to get an architecture diagram, gitingest.com for an LLM-readable dump, deepwiki.com for generated docs, or gitmcp.io to let your agent query the repo live over MCP. Pressing the period key on a GitHub repo opens it in browser VS Code.

item.title: Fish Audio phone agent — AI receptionist that gathers context then hands off
item.dc:creator: angus.sewell
item.description: A support line where a Fish Audio voice agent on a Twilio number discloses it is AI, asks consent to take notes, collects context into database tables, then calls you, briefs you and merges the call. Repeat callers get their history recalled. The agent never tries to resolve issues itself, avoiding Taco Bell-style failures.

item.title: Untitled "xy + t" clip — no identifiable subject
item.dc:creator: bradleytangonan
item.description: Caption reads only 'xy + t' with no speech or OCR; no identifiable subject.

item.title: Clipper outreach agent — Roy Lee's pay-per-view clipping army, automated
item.dc:creator: angus.sewell
item.description: Reverse-engineers Cluely founder Roy Lee's growth tactic of getting 700+ clipping accounts to post him on pay-per-view terms. An agent finds accounts your audience follows, scrapes suggested clipping accounts, pulls emails from bios, and drafts pitches pointing to raw footage and top-performing examples.

item.title: PBEMA TradingView indicator — trend-filter buy/sell line on the S&P 500
item.dc:creator: pb_ema
item.description: Promo for a free TradingView indicator (PBEMA): buy when price is above a moving-average line, sell below, claimed to outperform buy-and-hold on the S&P 500 since 1930 by sidestepping 2000 and 2008. The Munger attribution and the personal P&L claims are unverified, and the link is gated behind a comment.

item.title: Crypto wash trading — Ben McKenzie doc on fake volume and pump schemes
item.dc:creator: cbcgem
item.description: Clip from the documentary 'Everyone Is Lying to You for Money' where an insider explains wash trading: one actor trading between two accounts to walk prices up, luring outsiders before dumping. The interviewee claims 90-95% of crypto volume is fake and fewer than 20 people control the market.

item.title: Ozymandias read by Werner Herzog — archive and decay as film theme
item.dc:creator: sandboxfilms
item.description: Werner Herzog reads Shelley's 'Ozymandias' as the hook for Sandbox Films' documentary 'The Arc of Oblivion', about why humans build records that will inevitably fade. Worth it as a study in voice, pacing and pairing classic text with documentary imagery.

item.title: Qwen 27B at home — a dev ditching frontier labs for local models
item.dc:creator: cjtrowbridge
item.description: An ex-lab engineer argues the free Qwen 27B model, run locally or in the cloud, handles long complex tasks better than frontier labs. Also claims Blackwell chips, including their Jetson Thor boxes, have broken speculative decoding. Opinion-heavy with strong unverified claims.

item.title: Glenn Gould's humming — thinking music away from the piano
item.dc:creator: dailyhistoryclips
item.description: Glenn Gould hummed audibly on nearly every recording despite Columbia engineers' mic tricks. He traced it to practising under a vacuum cleaner's noise, which taught him to hear pieces internally and learn away from the instrument; the voice is the overflow, audible on the Goldberg Variations.
